inputs.text: A student in Jaipur had to use her graduation ceremony to raise administrative concerns in front of the Deputy Chief Minister. The fact that she felt public protest was the only way to be heard points to a deeper failure of accountability: institutions often protect their image and authority more readily than they respond to the people who depend on them. Calling her actions “inappropriate” polices how students speak instead of addressing why university leaders have remained silent. Students deserve meaningful ways to raise concerns without having to turn a milestone into a protest.
